title: Cover by current-minus-future warmth intervals crossed zero in four insect-catch samples in 2019-2020
abstract: We tested whether forest or canopy cover changed the warmth slope of insect catch during collection more than it changed the slope for weather shifted 14 days forward. We used 5,105 measured catches in Sweden and Madagascar in 2019-2020, in two periods per country. Models controlled trap, cover-specific season, rain and collection duration. Current-minus-future cover slope estimates were -0.008 and -0.060 in Sweden and +0.376 and +0.406 in Madagascar. All four adjusted intervals crossed zero. The cover unit was forest minus open habitat in Sweden and 50 percentage points of canopy in Madagascar; temperature was scaled by 5 C. All planned contrast checks also had intervals across zero. The result does not establish a repeated short-term cover response or show no buffering effect. One year per country, few time blocks, missing canopy, regional weather and selected catches limit inference. Catch mixes abundance, flight activity and capture. Pollution and climate trends were not tested. The package gives code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, numerical checks and a figure. Raw and record-level data remain external.

display.caption: Cover moderation of current and future temperature slopes and their direct difference in four country and period samples. Intervals use a four-test critical value. Only the four differences form the primary test family. Cover units differ between countries.
